A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Augmentation study. Their complete 35-page contents, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison despite the revised title and organization.

before.justification: V3 reports original experiments on sentence embeddings, image classification, and graph learning, together with supervised comparisons, ablations, transfer experiments, and representation analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds a regression analysis summarizing performance trends across modalities.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains layer-targeted dropout or PCA, optional stop-gradient, and augmentation of a random 50% of each batch. The expanded explanations do not introduce a different algorithm, architecture, objective, or layer-selection procedure.

E1.justification: Wikipedia/STS, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet100, COLLAB, IMDB-Multi, NCI1, and PROTEINS remain covered. Supervised learning, MLM-only experiments, and transfer between CIFAR datasets were already included in v3 and its appendices.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SimCSE, SimCLR, and GCL, along with the same initialization, freezing, dropout, PCA, and supervised reference configurations. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V4 Figure 9 introduces an aggregate analysis using z-score normalization with the original mean preserved and performance differences relative to baselines. The underlying benchmark splits, architectures, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 Figure 9 adds regression analysis of layer-depth trends across modalities, distinguishing supervision and stop-gradient conditions. Existing ablations and appendix analyses are retained; v3 Figure 5 becomes appendix Figure 14 rather than being removed.

E5.justification: Figure 9 newly introduces fitted regression estimates of layer-performance relationships. Existing uncertainty tables and error-bar plots are retained, including v3 Figure 21 as v4 Figure 22. No increased run counts, new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: V3 Table 1's separate STS point estimates, including averages 75.86 for SimCSE and 76.72 for DeepAug, are removed. V3 Table 2 is retained unchanged as v4 Table 1, including 75.61±0.924 and 76.56±0.161. Other matched benchmark results remain unchanged; Figure 9 adds aggregate fitted trends.

T1.justification: The contrastive-loss and augmentation equations, PCA expression, and Appendix E information-processing inequality are retained. The new co-adaptation paragraph provides conceptual explanation without introducing new formal mathematics, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: V4's abstract asserts that stop-gradient is critical for effective dropout augmentation, strengthening v3's presentation of an optional operation with benefits both with and without it. The principal claims about deeper layers, PCA alternatives, supervised-learning reversal, and co-adaptation remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds the explanation that stop-gradient prevents upstream layers from learning to undo perturbations and explicitly interprets high CKA as layer redundancy. Most explanations concerning information filtering, supervised invariances, and failure cases already appear in v3, including Appendix E.

D1.justification: V4 omits v3 Section 4's explicit statement that the three benchmark frameworks incorporate all-layer dropout with tuned rates. This reduces setting documentation without establishing an experimental change. Appendix architecture details, training budgets, augmentation settings, and provided code links are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Ulyanov et al. on Deep Image Prior, Zhang et al. on perceptual feature metrics, and Wu and Gu on convolutional-network dropout. These extend supporting context while preserving the principal positioning against uniform dropout and input-level augmentation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and substantial portions of the experimental discussion are rewritten. V4 organizes the narrative around two dropout questions, adds Section 5.4 Findings, removes the separate alignment/uniformity subsection heading, and reorganizes appendix prose around its results.

P2.justification: V4 adds regression Figure 9, moves v3 Figure 5 into Appendix A as Figure 14, removes v3 Table 1, and rearranges appendix figure/table placement. Existing plots, table formats, and graphical encodings are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer research questions, better placement of appendix explanations, and removal of the unexplained parallel STS score table make the retained evidence easier to assess. Figure 9 provides a useful additional synthesis. These modest gains outweigh limited losses in precision: the abstract makes a broader stop-gradient necessity claim than the qualified findings support, and one explicit baseline-setting statement disappears.
